children: ) found a technical foothold Thursday after sliding to a key moving average in the wake of the Federal Reserve’s latest rate decision.

On Wednesday, policymakers raised the federal funds rate by 25 basis points. The move triggered a sharp selloff that drove the index down to its 100-day moving average for the first time since April 13. That line, a widely watched gauge of intermediate trend, absorbed the decline. After briefly tagging the average, the S&P 500 ticked modestly higher off the low later in the session.
Overnight futures then extended the recovery. S&P 500 futures

were last seen rallying about 1.2% on Thursday’s session and standing roughly 1.8% above Wednesday’s low of day—the print that formed immediately after the Fed announcement. The rebound suggests some traders are treating the 100-day average as short-term support rather than a breakdown level.

The test does not resolve the larger policy debate. Officials signaled that further tightening remains on the table, and inflation has stayed elevated. For now, however, the market’s first reaction after the 100-day touch has been a bounce, not a clean break. How that average holds into the cash open will be the next technical checkpoint for bulls and bears alike.

title: S&P 500 kisses 100-day MA for first time since April; futures have since rebounded
